text: Add a user-by-tab categorical interaction so request surface can modulate each user's item ranking.
rationale: The request-context screen was the only positive feature-family screen (+0.00221 primary), while tab 0 remains weak on validation (GAUC 0.5419, nDCG@5 0.0577 over 13,726 rows). A user-by-tab term can vary within a user when request surfaces differ, unlike a user-only term.
exact_ablation: Append exactly one hashed categorical feature representing the pair (user_id, tab) to experiment 1's existing additive feature matrix; retain all existing fields, row-averaged BCE, optimizer, and early stopping unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: +0.001 to +0.004 from surface-specific user preference ordering.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: +0.000 to +0.003 if the interaction promotes relevant items on weak high-volume tabs.

text: Add a video-by-tab categorical interaction to learn surface-specific item appeal.
rationale: Tab is request-time available and positively screened as part of request context. The large validation weakness on tabs 0 and 6 indicates that a global video effect may be insufficient when the same candidate is scored on different surfaces.
exact_ablation: Append exactly one hashed categorical feature representing the pair (video_id, tab) to experiment 1's additive feature matrix; keep the existing individual fields, BCE objective, optimizer, and stopping rule unchanged.

expected_effect.nDCG@5: +0.001 to +0.004 because the ablation directly targets surface-specific top-rank errors.

text: Add a video-by-hour categorical interaction to capture time-dependent item relevance.
rationale: The request-context screen improved primary on every internal temporal-holdout day. Validation early-hour slices are particularly weak, including hour 3 GAUC 0.4894 and hour 4 GAUC 0.5318, leaving room for item appeal to vary by time of day.
exact_ablation: Append exactly one hashed categorical feature representing the pair (video_id, hour) to experiment 1's additive feature matrix; leave all other features and training settings unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: +0.000 to +0.003 from correcting hour-specific item misorders.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: +0.000 to +0.003 if relevant videos move into the top five in weak hour slices.

text: Add a tab-by-hour categorical interaction to model request-surface temporal regimes.
rationale: The positive request-context screen establishes temporal and surface information as useful, while both tab and early-hour validation slices show substantial ranking deficits. A compact context-only cross avoids untrusted metadata and outcome fields.
exact_ablation: Append exactly one categorical feature representing the pair (tab, hour) to experiment 1's additive feature matrix; retain user/video IDs, existing context fields, BCE, optimizer, and stopping unchanged.

expected_effect.nDCG@5: +0.000 to +0.003 if surface-hour context resolves top-five ties.

text: Replace the additive scorer with a low-rank factorization-machine scorer over the existing five fields.
rationale: Experiment 1's additive model reached GAUC 0.6689 but nDCG@5 only 0.5370. Its score has no learned feature interactions, so a low-rank interaction scorer supplies a distinct within-user ordering mechanism without introducing new data sources.
exact_ablation: Replace experiment 1's linear additive logit with a rank-8 factorization-machine logit over exactly user_id, video_id, tab, hour, and weekday; preserve the same data split, fields, row-averaged BCE, optimizer schedule, and early-stopping procedure.

expected_effect.GAUC: +0.001 to +0.005 from user-item and item-context interactions.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: +0.001 to +0.005 if interactions improve ordering near the top of each user's candidates.

text: Replace pointwise BCE with within-user sampled RankNet loss on training impressions.
rationale: The official objective is within-user ranking, yet experiment 1 was trained with pointwise BCE. The validation pattern of moderate nDCG@5 and weak surface slices supports testing a directly ordering-oriented objective, while experiment 2 shows that merely reweighting pointwise BCE was harmful.
exact_ablation: Replace row-averaged BCE in experiment 1 with RankNet logistic loss over positive-negative pairs sampled only among each user's training-split impressions, using at most four uniformly sampled negatives per positive and equal weight per user; keep the scorer and features unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: +0.001 to +0.006 because the loss directly trains positive-versus-negative order within user.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: -0.001 to +0.004; broad user-history pairs may not preferentially correct top-five inversions.

text: Add an nDCG@5-weighted LambdaRank-style pair term to the existing BCE objective.
rationale: Experiment 1 has stronger GAUC than nDCG@5, and the medium-frequency-item slice in experiment 2 has GAUC 0.7213 but nDCG@5 only 0.2444. That separation motivates a top-five-focused correction rather than another calibration-oriented pointwise change.
exact_ablation: Change only the loss to row-averaged BCE plus a lambda=0.25 detached nDCG@5-swap-weighted RankNet term over positive-negative pairs within each user's training impressions; keep experiment 1's scorer, features, optimizer, and checkpointing unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: -0.001 to +0.003 because top-five weighting can trade broad pairwise order for head ranking.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: +0.001 to +0.006 if top-rank positive-negative inversions are common.

text: Replace pointwise BCE with per-user ListNet top-one loss over training impressions.
rationale: The principal shortfall is top-five quality rather than only global discrimination. A listwise objective is materially different from experiment 2's inverse-user-count BCE and explicitly makes candidates compete within user groups.
exact_ablation: Replace experiment 1's BCE with ListNet top-one cross-entropy computed separately over every user's complete training-impression group, excluding all-negative and all-positive groups from the listwise term; retain features and scorer unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: -0.002 to +0.003 because list normalization can weaken broad pairwise discrimination.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: +0.001 to +0.005 if list competition better promotes positives near each user's head.

text: Add a causal prior user-video long-view affinity feature for repeated item exposure.
rationale: Validation rare and medium-frequency items have much weaker nDCG@5 than the global score, so repeated exposure history may provide candidate-specific preference information. The existing user-author history screen was negative, making this a deliberately narrow and uncertain user-item alternative rather than a broad history rollout.
exact_ablation: Append exactly one discretized causal feature: the smoothed long-view rate for prior training events with the same (user_id, video_id), emitting the feature before updating state with the current row and using an explicit unseen bucket; retain experiment 1's scorer and BCE unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: -0.001 to +0.003; repeated-item affinity may order familiar candidates better, but the negative author-affinity screen is adverse evidence.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: -0.001 to +0.003, with any gain expected mainly where repeated candidate exposure exists.

text: Select checkpoints by validation primary rather than the current validation-GAUC proxy.
rationale: The fixed selection objective averages GAUC and nDCG@5, but experiment 1 checkpointing uses only a GAUC proxy. Its nDCG@5 is materially below GAUC, and experiment 2 demonstrated that a presumed GAUC-alignment change can reduce both official metrics.
exact_ablation: Change only checkpoint selection: after each epoch, retain the checkpoint with the highest official validation primary=(GAUC+nDCG@5)/2 instead of the highest validation-GAUC proxy; preserve experiment 1's model, fields, BCE updates, seed, and epoch budget.

expected_effect.GAUC: -0.001 to +0.001 because selection may accept a small GAUC trade-off.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: +0.000 to +0.003 because checkpoint choice is aligned to the top-five component.

text: Use frequency-adaptive L2 regularization for video-ID weights to reduce sparse-item overfitting.
rationale: Item-frequency slices show sharply lower top-five quality for rare and medium-frequency videos despite medium items having strong GAUC. Frequency-adaptive shrinkage is a narrowly targeted regularization change that can stabilize item scores without using prohibited aggregate snapshots.
exact_ablation: Change only regularization by applying L2 to each video_id weight scaled as 1/sqrt(training impression count for that video_id), with counts computed from the training split only; all non-video weights retain experiment 1's existing L2 and all other training settings remain fixed.

expected_effect.GAUC: -0.001 to +0.002; additional shrinkage can improve tail generalization but may damp useful item distinctions.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: +0.000 to +0.003 if reduced sparse-item variance improves top-five stability.

text: Lower the Adam learning rate from 0.01 to 0.005 for the existing experiment-1 model.
rationale: The latest loss change reduced primary by 0.00452 against experiment 1, so a low-risk optimization-control candidate can test whether the simple additive model's held-out ranking is sensitive to update magnitude without adding features or altering the target. This is intentionally low priority because no measured underfitting signature establishes a likely gain.
exact_ablation: Change only the learning_rate in experiment 1's configuration from 0.01 to 0.005; preserve the model, fields, row-averaged BCE, batch size, seed, maximum epochs, and patience.

expected_effect.GAUC: -0.001 to +0.002 depending on whether smaller updates improve temporal generalization.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: -0.001 to +0.002; slower fitting may either stabilize or underfit head ordering within the fixed epoch budget.
